It contains no biographical content about López Obrador and no economic policy content of any kind.","exclusion_reason":"website navigation header - no biographical content, no economic policy content, no relevance to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0002","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0002 is a political biography overview covering López Obrador's charismatic leadership style, combative discourse, 2018 electoral victory with 53.2% of votes, and early political origins from the left-wing nationalist tradition of the PRD. Contains no specific economic policy content, no enacted fiscal or budgetary measures, no appointments of economic professionals, no regulatory or competition frameworks, and no executed budget outcomes.","exclusion_reason":"general political biography overview - contains electoral history, leadership style descriptions, party affiliation history; no substantive economic policy proposals, no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory frameworks, no executed budget outcomes relevant to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0003","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0003 covers the 2006 presidential election dispute with Felipe Calderón, López Obrador's allegations of electoral fraud, his declaration as 'legitimate president,' and the international community's recognition of Calderón's victory. Contains no specific economic policy content, no enacted fiscal measures, no professional appointments, no regulatory or competition frameworks.","exclusion_reason":"2006 electoral dispute and post-electoral rebellion narrative - political conflict description, fraud allegations, 'Gobierno alterno' formation; no substantive economic policy content, no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory or competition frameworks relevant to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0004","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0004 covers the 2012 electoral defeat to Enrique Peña Nieto, López Obrador's fraud allegations and legal challenge, his break from the PRD, and the founding of MORENA as an opposition movement. Contains no specific economic policy content beyond general opposition to neoliberal reforms, no enacted fiscal measures, no professional appointments, no regulatory or competition frameworks.","exclusion_reason":"2012 electoral defeat, PRD split, and MORENA founding narrative - party political conflict description, electoral fraud allegations; no substantive economic policy proposals, no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory or competition frameworks relevant to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0005","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0006","unit-0004"],"explanation":"Unit-0005 contains the substantive 2018 electoral program (Proyecto 2018 / Juntos Haremos Historia) with specific, concrete economic policy proposals directly addressing all ten 5B questions: (5B.1) 'austeridad republicana' to reorient public resources from current spending to investment without tax increases; (5B.2) professional appointments implied by competence-based governance promises; (5B.3) macroeconomic discipline commitments with peso flotación; (5B.4) increase domestic gasoline production to reduce imports and lower prices, energy and food self-sufficiency with guaranteed prices for local producers; (5B.5) 'erradicar la corrupción política dando ejemplo' from Los Pinos, explicit anti-corruption commitment; (5B.6) social programs targeting poverty and vulnerable groups, 'pacificar' Mexico in three years, infrastructure investment; (5B.7) transparency and anti-corruption framing; (5B.8) targeted social programs for vulnerable populations, indigenous peoples, pension increases; (5B.9) fuel price reduction through domestic production, border solidarity with migrants; (5B.10) overall 'transformación' agenda. This is the most substantive economic policy content in the document."}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0006","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0007"],"explanation":"Unit-0006 contains López Obrador's explicit characterization of his platform as 'socialdemocracia pragmática que asume las nociones orthodoxas del libre mercado, la estabilidad macroeconómica, la disciplina presupuestaria y la flotación del peso' while rejecting privatization and prioritizing national production. It contains the key economic governance framework directly relevant to all ten 5B questions: (5B.1) rejection of neoliberalism, prioritization of national production; (5B.2) reference to competent governance and economic professionals; (5B.3) explicit commitment to macroeconomic stability, fiscal discipline, and peso flotación; (5B.4) rejection of privatization of strategic sectors; (5B.5) promise to end corruption and privileges of former presidents 'sin venganza ni odio'; (5B.6) promises of justice without vengeance and governance respect for legal order; (5B.8) conservative stance on social issues combined with progressive economic promises. Unit-0006 is adjacent to unit-0005 (same economic policy program discussion) and unit-0007 (transitions to security/border issues). Note: document coverage ends August 2018, before the December 2018 inauguration, so all content represents pre-presidency proposals rather than executed policies."}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0007","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0007 discusses the USMCA trade agreement, border migration caravans, and US-Mexico relations under Trump. Contains no specific economic policy content regarding fiscal rules, professional appointments, competition frameworks, anti-corruption enforcement, infrastructure quality, economic information transparency, distributional incidence, or shock response mechanisms. Migration and trade agreement discussions are tangentially related to economic conditions but do not constitute substantive evidence for any 5B question.","exclusion_reason":"USMCA trade agreement, border migration caravan crisis, and US-Mexico diplomatic tensions under Trump; no substantive economic policy content relevant to any 5B question - trade agreement mentioned as context but not analyzed for its economic governance implications"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0008","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0008 begins the detailed biographical section (section 1) covering López Obrador's family background, childhood in Tabasco, the 1969 accidental shooting death of his younger brother José Ramón, move to Palenque, and early life. Contains no economic policy content whatsoever.","exclusion_reason":"early biographical section - family origins, childhood in Tabasco, accidental shooting death of brother; no economic policy content, no relevance to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0009","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0009 covers López Obrador's 1972 enrollment at UNAM Faculty of Political Sciences, his early PRI activism, and his first political work organizing Carlos Pellicer Cámara's 1976 Senate campaign. Contains no economic policy content, no enacted fiscal measures, no professional appointments, no regulatory frameworks.","exclusion_reason":"early political career biography - UNAM enrollment, PRI membership, first campaign activism in 1976; no economic policy content, no relevance to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0010","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0010 covers López Obrador's appointment as delegate of the National Indigenist Institute (INI) in La Chontalpa, direction of Sectoral Studies in the state secretariat, teaching positions at Universidad Autónoma de Tabasco, marriage to Rocío Beltrán Medina, and birth of three sons. Contains no economic policy content.","exclusion_reason":"early government career biography - INI delegate position, teaching, family formation; no economic policy content, no relevance to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0011","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0011 covers López Obrador's role in the 1982 campaign of Enrique González Pedrero for governor of Tabasco, appointment as director of CEPES, and his January 1983 designation as president of the Tabasco PRI State Executive Committee. Contains no economic policy content beyond general party organizational work.","exclusion_reason":"PRI party career biography - campaign work for González Pedrero, CEPES directorship, Tabasco PRI presidency; no substantive economic policy content, no relevance to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0012","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0012 covers the 1988 electoral fraud allegations, López Obrador's participation in the Democratic Current (Corriente Democrática) within the PRI, theFront of Democratic National (FDN) coalition, and the alleged computer system collapse during the presidential election. Contains no economic policy content.","exclusion_reason":"1988 electoral fraud narrative and Democratic Current within PRI; no substantive economic policy content, no relevance to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0013","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0013 covers the founding of the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) in May 1989, López Obrador's role as PRD president in Tabasco, and his organization of the 'exodus for democracy' march in 1991-1992. Contains no economic policy content.","exclusion_reason":"PRD founding and early party political career - 1989 party formation, 1991-1992 democratic march; no substantive economic policy content, no relevance to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0014","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0014 covers López Obrador's second failed gubernatorial campaign in Tabasco (1994), his allegations of electoral fraud against Roberto Madrazo, the 1995 democratic caravan, and the creation of the National Democratic Alliance. Contains no substantive economic policy content beyond general opposition to PRI governance.","exclusion_reason":"1994 Tabasco gubernatorial campaign, electoral fraud allegations, democratic caravan; no substantive economic policy content, no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no regulatory frameworks relevant to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0015","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0015 covers López Obrador's 1996 election as president of the PRD National Executive Committee (CEN) with 73.9% of votes, his leftist positioning within the party, and his role in protesting PEMEX management in Tabasco. Contains no substantive economic policy content.","exclusion_reason":"1996 PRD national presidency election, party leftist positioning, PEMEX protest; no substantive economic policy content, no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no regulatory frameworks relevant to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0016","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0016 covers the PRD's 1997 electoral successes including Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas' election as first elected head of government of Mexico City, PRD's gain of 38 of 66 seats in the DF Assembly, and López Obrador's delivery of the party presidency in April 1999 to Pablo Gómez. Contains no substantive economic policy content.","exclusion_reason":"1997-1999 PRD electoral successes and party leadership transitions; no substantive economic policy content, no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no regulatory frameworks relevant to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0017","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0017 covers López Obrador's publication of the FOBAPROA investigation findings and his book 'Fobaproa, expediente abierto,' characterizing the fund as 'el fraude más grande de la historia después de La Conquista.' Contains reference to financial sector critique but no enacted economic policy, no professional appointments, no regulatory frameworks, no executed budgets.","exclusion_reason":"FOBAPROA critique and 1999 publication - opposition critique of 1994-1995 bank rescue fund; no enacted economic policy during López Obrador's own governance, no professional appointments, no regulatory frameworks, no executed budget outcomes relevant to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0018","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0018 covers López Obrador's November 1999 primary victory to be PRD candidate for head of government of Mexico City, his July 2000 electoral triumph winning the DF head of government position with 34.5% of votes, and the context of Vicente Fox's historic PAN victory over the PRI. Contains no substantive economic policy content.","exclusion_reason":"1999-2000 Mexico City head of government electoral campaign and victory; no substantive economic policy content, no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no regulatory frameworks relevant to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0019","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0019 covers López Obrador's December 2000 inauguration as head of government of Mexico City, his personal style of governance described as voluntaristic, austere, and committed to social causes, his daily morning press conferences (las mañaneras), and his indexed popularity in surveys. Contains no substantive economic policy content with specific policy proposals, enacted measures, or budget outcomes.","exclusion_reason":"personal governance style description, morning press conferences, public perception; no substantive enacted economic policy with specific fiscal/tax/monetary measures, no professional economic appointments documented, no regulatory frameworks enacted, no executed budget outcomes documented for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0020","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0020 covers López Obrador's media strategy, his connection with working classes through accessible language, his research and analysis capabilities shown in historical essays, his nicknames 'El Peje' and 'AMLO,' and mixed assessments of his municipal management results. Contains general governance characterization without specific enacted economic policies, fiscal measures, professional appointments, or budget outcomes.","exclusion_reason":"communication style, media strategy, public image; no substantive enacted economic policy with specific fiscal/tax/monetary measures, no professional economic appointments documented, no regulatory frameworks enacted, no executed budget outcomes documented for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0021","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0021 covers the results of López Obrador's Mexico City government: vigorous public works campaign for infrastructure improvement, social protection programs including the Universal Food Pension for the Elderly (Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores), and the decision not to implement the Popular Insurance health program. Contains general descriptions of social programs without specific fiscal amounts, budgetary execution details, professional appointments of economic technocrats, or regulatory frameworks for competition or anti-corruption.","exclusion_reason":"Mexico City government results - social programs, infrastructure works; general descriptions without specific enacted fiscal measures, no professional economic appointments documented, no regulatory competition frameworks enacted, no executed budget outcomes with measurable results relevant to any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0022","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0022 covers the March 2004 video scandal (videoescándalo) involving illegal video recordings of PRD politicians including René Bejarano and Carlos Ímaz Gispert receiving money from businessman Carlos Ahumada Kurtz, and their subsequent arrests for fraud and money laundering. Contains political corruption narrative but no enacted anti-corruption rules, no enforcement against politically connected actors by López Obrador, and no specific economic governance frameworks.","exclusion_reason":"2004 video scandal and corruption allegations against PRD subordinates; corruption narrative but not evidence of enacted anti-corruption rules, professional economic appointments, regulatory competition frameworks, or executed budget outcomes for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0023","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0023 continues the video scandal narrative, López Obrador's delayed and tepid reaction, his political counterattack attributing the scandal to a 'conspiracy' by former president Salinas, panist Fernández de Cevallos, and the Fox government. Contains political analysis but no enacted anti-corruption measures, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory frameworks, no fiscal or budgetary policies.","exclusion_reason":"political conspiracy theory in response to video scandal; no enacted anti-corruption rules, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory competition frameworks, no executed budget outcomes for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0024","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0024 covers the May 2004 PGR request for congressional removal of immunity (desafuero) against López Obrador related to a land expropriation dispute in Cuajimalpa from 2000-2001, and PRD accusations of political persecution. Contains legal dispute narrative but no enacted fiscal, tax, monetary, or regulatory policies, no professional economic appointments, no anti-corruption enforcement actions by López Obrador.","exclusion_reason":"2004 desafuero judicial process and political persecution allegations; no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory competition frameworks, no anti-corruption enforcement for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0025","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0025 covers the August 2004 demonstration of 200,000 PRD supporters in the Zócalo, López Obrador's October 2004 book 'Un proyecto alternativo de nación,' and the November 2004 dismissal of Marcelo Ebrard as Mexico City Public Security Secretary following the Tláhuac lynching incident. Contains political mobilization narrative and personnel change but no enacted economic policies, fiscal measures, regulatory frameworks, or budget outcomes.","exclusion_reason":"political demonstrations, 2004 book publication, Ebrard dismissal; no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory competition frameworks, no executed budget outcomes for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0026","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0026 covers the April 2005 congressional vote approving López Obrador's desafuero (360-127), his call for peaceful civil resistance movement with hundreds of thousands of supporters, and the DF Assembly's constitutional challenge to the Supreme Court. Contains political confrontation narrative but no enacted economic policies, fiscal measures, professional appointments, or regulatory frameworks.","exclusion_reason":"2005 congressional desafuero vote and civil resistance mobilization; no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory competition frameworks, no executed budget outcomes for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0027","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0027 covers the May 2005 resolution where the PGR failed to get a judge to initiate proceedings against López Obrador, President Fox's acceptance of the attorney general's resignation, and the May 2005 withdrawal of charges. Contains political-legal resolution narrative but no enacted economic policies, fiscal measures, professional appointments, or regulatory frameworks.","exclusion_reason":"desafuero resolution, charges withdrawn; no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory competition frameworks, no executed budget outcomes for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0028","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0028 covers López Obrador's July 2005 departure from the DF head of government position, his uncontested PRD presidential primary candidacy, and his December 2005 formal proclamation as candidate of the Por el Bien de Todos coalition. Contains electoral positioning narrative but no enacted economic policies, fiscal measures, professional appointments, or regulatory frameworks.","exclusion_reason":"PRD presidential primary, candidacy proclamation; no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory competition frameworks, no executed budget outcomes for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0029","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0029 covers the 2006 presidential campaign dynamics, Calderón's accusations against López Obrador regarding documents implicating him in nepotism and abuse of power when director of BANOBRAS and Energy Secretary, and López Obrador's accusations against Calderón regarding FOBAPROA. Contains electoral accusations and political attacks but no enacted economic policies, fiscal measures, professional appointments, or regulatory frameworks.","exclusion_reason":"2006 campaign accusations and attacks; no enacted fiscal/tax/monetary policy, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory competition frameworks, no executed budget outcomes for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0030","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0030 covers the 2006 coalition program 'Por el Bien de Todos' with its anti-corruption, anti-neoliberalism platform, promises to halve presidential salary, and investigation of FOBAPROA through a Truth Commission. Contains campaign platform mentions but no enacted economic policies during López Obrador's own governance, no executed budgets, no professional appointments. This is opposition rhetoric rather than governance evidence.","exclusion_reason":"2006 campaign program - anti-corruption and anti-neoliberal rhetoric; opposition program not enacted governance, no executed budgets, no professional economic appointments, no regulatory competition frameworks during López Obrador's own administration for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0031","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0031 covers the coalition's proposed social development programs extending public services to marginalized areas, support for vulnerable groups, productive sector development in agriculture, tourism, and public works, and the commitment to constitutional salary levels. Contains campaign promises but no enacted economic policies, no executed budgets during López Obrador's own governance, no professional appointments documented.","exclusion_reason":"2006 campaign social development promises; opposition program not enacted governance, no executed budgets during López Obrador's own administration, no professional economic appointments, no enacted fiscal/monetary policy for any 5B question"}, {"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0032","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0032 covers López Obrador's distancing from Venezuelan President Chávez and the PRD's distance from Bolivarian strategy for Latin America, and the international relations context of the 2006 campaign.
